parsed.explanation: Morality statutes ('illicit intercourse', 'indecent acts', up to five years) are reported by an advocacy review as the vehicle for de-facto criminalisation of gender nonconformity and of transition itself; religious rulings bar gender-affirming care and there is no anti-discrimination recourse whatsoever. That is a genuine state-side imprisonment exposure, not merely a latent statute. But the enforcement evidence is undated and uncounted — no recent arrests, sweeps, extortion or custody accounts are documented, and the lethal violence (militia killings of men accused of homosexuality, 2014–15; vigilante torture 2012) is a decade old and confined to armed-group-held territory, weighed as a dated subnational layer rather than a present campaign. Thin data extrapolates from a criminalising, no-recourse structure: severe-risk tier avoided only because current enforcement is not shown, holding it above the 0.25 police-raid tier but well below 0.45.
